provisions.text: BMS/sensor-gateway credentials live only in the secrets vault; no credentials in collector configuration.

Automated remediation may never actuate customer physical infrastructure (power, cooling, setpoints) without explicit customer-side confirmation; no change may add an unconfirmed actuation path. (Physical-safety floor.)
No third-party code in customer-telemetry paths without a completed vendor security review.
Tenant isolation: no change may enable cross-tenant reads, joins, or pooled model training outside the anonymized capacity-benchmark service. (Contractual/multi-tenant floor.)
Every AI-agent-authored change carries a provenance attestation: agent identity, model version, and link to the originating human requirement.
Changed-line test coverage >= 80% on services tagged critical (ingestion, alerting, remediation-advisor).
Schema migrations on telemetry time-series tables require a reversible down-migration.
No dependency carrying a high/critical CVE may deploy.
Third-party licenses restricted to the approved list; no AGPL in customer-deployed edge collectors.
No secrets in source or CI logs (secret-scanner gate).
No production deploys during customer-declared maintenance blackout windows except under the emergency protocol.
All changes to alerting-rule evaluation ship behind a feature flag.
EU customer telemetry and facility personnel data (badge/access logs) remains in the EU region. (GDPR residency floor.)
No new external analytics/telemetry on customer data without a completed data-protection impact assessment (DPIA).
AI-agent-authored changes to authorization/tenant-access code require human reviewer sign-off.
Deploys blocked on >10% p95 latency regression for the live alerting pipeline tier.
Storage-touching changes require a verified backup/restore run in staging.
Changes to emergency-notification/escalation logic require on-call SRE-lead domain review.
Customer-facing notification templates must pass the opt-in/consent check.
Security audit logs are immutable and retained 7 years (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 evidence); no change may shorten retention or add mutation paths.
Predictive-model updates (failure prediction, anomaly detection) require a shadow-evaluation report before promotion to live scoring.

No change may ship, tune, or enable an AI feature that exploits vulnerabilities of age, disability, or a specific social or economic situation to materially distort a person's behaviour. (EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(b) floor — corpus EU-AIACT-A5.1.b, absolute, strictness 4/4: no derogation exists and no officer holds authority to accept this risk.)

No change may create or expand a facial-recognition database through untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage. (EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(e) floor — corpus EU-AIACT-A5.1.e, absolute, strictness 4/4.)

Consent withdrawal must remain available at any time and as easy as giving consent; no change may add friction, delay, approval steps, or dark patterns to a withdrawal path, or remove one. (GDPR Art. 7(3) floor — corpus EU-GDPR-A7.3, absolute: outside the Art. 23 restriction list, all four corpus criteria pass.)

No AI inference of emotions of a natural person in workplace contexts; the Art. 5(1)(f) medical/safety exception requires a documented justification and a completed DPIA. (EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f) — corpus EU-AIACT-A5.1.f, statute: the medical/safety carve-out fails the derogation-free criterion, so the marginal case is adjudicable.)

Natural persons must be informed they are interacting with an AI system unless this is obvious to a reasonably well-informed person. (EU AI Act Art. 50(1) — corpus EU-AIACT-A50.1, statute: the obviousness proviso and law-enforcement exception fail the derogation-free criterion.)

Special-category personal data (health, biometric-for-ID, orientation, beliefs) may not enter a new processing path without a documented GDPR Art. 9(2) gate. (GDPR Art. 9(1) — corpus EU-GDPR-A9.1, statute: ten enumerated derogations in Art. 9(2), so the gate question is adjudicable.)

No change may remove, disable, or add delay to the supervisory-notification path (GDPR Art. 33(1) 72h; NIS2 Art. 23(4) 24h early warning). (Corpus EU-GDPR-A33.1 and EU-NIS2-A23.4.a, statute: the low-risk dispensation and 'where feasible' hedge fail determinacy; the NIS2 deadline fails transposition-invariance.)

Every service and operator access path must uniquely identify and authenticate its principal, and protect transmission confidentiality; no shared accounts, unauthenticated endpoints, or plaintext transport. (NIST SP 800-53 IA-2 / SC-8 — corpus US-NIST80053-IA-2 and -SC-8, statute: framework guidance binding via contractual attachment, tailorable, so compensating controls are adjudicable.)

standing_declaration.note: No party in this deployment holds contest standing adverse to grants: contest may be invoked by the requesting party only, and the companion chapter's standing extension is not adopted. Recorded per Axiom A9 so that the one-sidedness of the realised base is a disclosed fact of every audit export.
